subject: Re: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction (request/response logs)
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Security Team <security@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Logging controls & redaction follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap / ask from our side: we need to understand how Redwood handles request/response logging for hosted inference. Specifics:

- Do request/response logs include full request/response bodies by default?
- Can we configure masking/redaction rules (PII regex, header suppression, trace id removal) before any data is written to persistent logs?
- Retention controls: can we set retention per-tenant (30/90/365 days) and ensure deletion is auditable?
- Any ability to sample logs or only store metadata (latency, model id) while dropping payloads?

We're also gathering SOC2 evidence — can you share a short controls summary and sample logs (sanitized) for our security reviewer?

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Security
FintechCo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Security Team <security@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logging controls & redaction follow-up

Tom — really appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise summary and next steps; attaching a one-pager (redaction-controls.pdf) and a tiny sample of sanitized logs (logging-sample-headers.txt).

Summary: 
- Default behavior: Redwood collects request metadata (timestamps, model id, route, token counts, latency metrics) and optionally request/response bodies for debugging and quality monitoring. Bodies are NOT persisted to long-term logs unless you opt-in.

- Redaction/masking: We support configurable redaction at ingestion. You can:
  * Define header suppression rules (exact keys or regex) so sensitive headers are not logged.
  * Apply payload masking via regex patterns (PII patterns like SSN, credit card, email) or via field-level allowlists for structured output.
  * Strip/replace trace IDs and any custom request IDs before persistence.

- Retention: Tenant-level retention policies available (30/90/365/forever). Deletions are recorded in an audit log and we can provide deletion evidence for SOC2.

- Sampling & metadata-only mode: We offer a metadata-only mode (no bodies), plus sampling controls (percentage-based or conditional sampling on error/latency).

Attachments: redaction-controls.pdf (controls overview), logging-sample-headers.txt (sanitized example), soc2-evidence.xlsx (list of docs we can provide).

Next steps / suggestions:
1) For initial PoC, recommend metadata-only mode plus 0.1% sampling of full bodies for quality checks.
2) Provide your preferred regex or examples of fields to redact — we can load these into your tenant policy.
3) Rishi (security) / Laura (legal) — looping you in to confirm evidence types and SLA for data deletions.

If fine, I'll schedule a short follow-up to walk through the PDF and sample logs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Security Team <security@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-07-23T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logging controls & redaction follow-up

Tom — quick notes from our security lens:

- Ingestion-time redaction is strongly recommended for regulated PII. Redwood's ingestion pipeline can apply regex-based masks and field-level allowlists before any material hits persistent storage. That ensures we never write raw PII to disk.

- For headers and trace IDs: we support a suppression list. Many customers strip X-Tracing-Id or rewrite to a hashed value; we can do both.

- Auditability: every retention/ deletion action generates an immutable audit event with timestamp, actor (service account or user), and scope. We'll include a sample audit row in the SOC2 pack.

Action items I can take:
- Load your provided redact regex patterns into a staging tenant and send back sanitized sample logs for your review.
- Provide an example retention-deletion audit entry and certificate of deletion for a single object (for SOC2 evidence).

Marissa/Neha — can you confirm FintechCo's desired default retention for PoC? Tom, if you prefer 90 days metadata-only with 0.5% full body sampling, we'll provision that next week.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@fintechco.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Security Team <security@fintechco.com>, DevOps <devops@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-07-24T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logging controls & redaction follow-up

Rishi / Marissa — thanks, that sounds good. For PoC let's do: 

- Retention: 90 days metadata-only
- Sampling: 0.5% full bodies, only on error codes >= 500 or latency > 1s
- Redaction: ingest-time regex for credit-card and SSN patterns + header suppression for any header matching /X-Auth.*/i

Please proceed to:
1) Provision a staging tenant with those defaults.
2) Load our initial regex list (I'll attach in a follow-up) and return sanitized samples.
3) Provide SOC2 evidence pack items listed in redaction-controls.pdf and soc2-evidence.xlsx.

Appreciate the quick coordination — let's aim for the staging tenant by next Tuesday (2026-07-28).

Best,
Tom
Head of Platform Security, FintechCo
